title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 28 (Rules applicable to substance of dispute)

content.overview: Where the place of arbitration is in India, in other than international commercial arbitration the tribunal shall decide the dispute in accordance with the substantive law for the time being in force in India. In international commercial arbitration, the tribunal applies the rules of law designated by the parties; failing designation, the rules it considers appropriate. The tribunal shall decide in accordance with the terms of the contract and take into account applicable trade usages. Decision ex aequo et bono or as amiable compositeur requires express authorisation.
content.glance: Domestic: Indian substantive law. ICA: party-designated rules, else tribunal chooses. Contract terms and trade usages apply. Ex aequo et bono only if authorised.
content.study: Non-ICA India-seated: Indian substantive law. ICA: party-designated rules of law, else appropriate rules. Always decide in accordance with the contract and take trade usages into account. Equitable decision-making needs express authorisation.

sections.heading: Domestic / non-ICA
sections.body: Substantive law for the time being in force in India where place is in India and not ICA.

sections.heading: International commercial arbitration
sections.body: Party-designated rules of law; failing designation, rules the tribunal considers appropriate.

sections.heading: Contract and trade usages
sections.body: Decide in accordance with the contract; take into account applicable trade usages.

provisions.title: Rules applicable to substance of dispute

examples.title: Application of aca-s-28
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the provision produce the consequence described in the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage aca-s-28?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements stated in the text.

distinctions.title: Scope of aca-s-28
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: aca-s-28 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What law applies under section 28 in a domestic India-seated arbitration?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The substantive law for the time being in force in India.

examTips: Separate domestic and ICA regimes; contract terms and trade usages always matter.

enhancement.definition: Section 28 governs the rules applicable to the substance of the dispute.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Domestic: Indian law. ICA: designated or appropriate rules. Contract and trade usages. Ex aequo et bono only if authorised.

tenMark.point: State the rule for non-ICA arbitrations seated in India
tenMark.application: Decide in accordance with the substantive law for the time being in force in India.

tenMark.point: State the rule for international commercial arbitration
tenMark.application: Apply the rules of law designated by the parties; failing designation, the rules the tribunal considers appropriate.

tenMark.point: Require decision in accordance with the contract
tenMark.application: The tribunal shall decide only in accordance with the terms of the contract and take into account applicable trade usages.

tenMark.point: State the condition for ex aequo et bono / amiable compositeur
tenMark.application: Only if the parties have expressly authorised the tribunal to do so.

sixteenMark.application: Separates domestic and ICA choice-of-law regimes and preserves contract terms.

sixteenMark.point: Apply party designation in an ICA problem
sixteenMark.application: Identify the designated rules of law and apply them to the substance.
Tribunal selects appropriate rules having regard to the circumstances.

sixteenMark.point: Analyse contract terms and trade usages
sixteenMark.application: These constrain the tribunal even after the applicable law is identified.
Identify the applicable substantive rules and any authorised equitable mandate.
